evals.prompt: We're a SaaS vendor and want each customer isolated in one IdentityServer deployment: separate clients, grants, and issuer. Should I use Multi-Issuer or something else?
evals.expected_output: Spaces (licensed preview add-on) isolate config + operational data per tenant; Multi-Issuer only varies iss; tenant acr hint is only a hint.
assertions: Recommends Spaces for isolating configuration and operational data per tenant on top of Duende Storage
States Multi-Issuer only changes the iss claim and does not separate data
States the tenant: acr_values hint is an untrusted client-supplied hint that cannot select a space
Notes Spaces are a licensed add-on in preview and require Duende Storage

evals.prompt: Set up Duende.Spaces with SQLite so tenant 'Acme' is served at https://login.example.com/t/acme. Include the middleware order and provisioning code.
evals.expected_output: AddSpaces, SpacesOptions, ForwardedHeaders, MigrateAsync, ISpaceAdmin idempotent create with SpaceMatchPattern, UseForwardedHeaders -> UseSpaceResolution -> UseRouting -> UseIdentityServer.
assertions: Adds Duende.Spaces and Duende.Storage.Sqlite with --prerelease
Registers AddStorage(...), AddConfigurationStorage(), AddOperationalStorage() and builder.Services.AddSpaces()
Creates the space with ISpaceAdmin.CreateAsync using CreateSpaceConfiguration and SpaceMatchPattern { Origin, Path = "/acme" } after querying by name first
Orders middleware UseForwardedHeaders, UseSpaceResolution, then UseRouting before UseIdentityServer
Configures ForwardedHeaders with known proxies/networks rather than trusting all sources
Does not set IdentityServerOptions.IssuerUri

evals.prompt: After enabling Spaces, all spaces return the same issuer in discovery. We set options.IssuerUri = "https://login.example.com". Why and how to fix?
evals.expected_output: A fixed IssuerUri makes every space return the same iss; leave unset so issuer is inferred from origin + path base.
assertions: Explains setting IssuerUri forces the same issuer/iss for every space
Recommends leaving IssuerUri unset so the issuer is inferred from each request's origin and path base
Notes that data and discovery endpoints remain separate per space even with a fixed IssuerUri
Mentions the same applies to Multi-Issuer

evals.prompt: Requests to unknown tenant paths return 404 in our Spaces deployment and a colleague wants to set FallbackToDefault = true so they go to the default space. Is that wise?
evals.expected_output: Strict 404 is safer; enable fallback only intentionally; default space uses pool 0.
assertions: Explains that by default unmatched requests (and requests with the /t prefix but no match) return 404
Warns FallbackToDefault should only be enabled when serving unmatched host/path from the default space is an intentional part of the isolation model
States a strict 404 is safer for multi-tenant deployments
Mentions the default space uses data pool 0

evals.prompt: What does Spaces NOT isolate? We plan to share signing keys, Data Protection keys and a Redis cache across spaces and keep one shared user database.
evals.expected_output: Spaces isolate persisted data only; review signing credentials, Data Protection, caches, telemetry, rate limits, custom services, user databases not using IStorageFactory; User Management is space-aware by default.
assertions: States Spaces isolate persisted data but not process-level dependencies
Lists signing credentials, ASP.NET Core Data Protection, external caches, telemetry, rate limits and custom services as things to review
Notes shared signing credentials reduce cryptographic separation between spaces
Notes user databases are not space-aware unless they use the shared IStorageFactory, while Duende User Management data is routed per space by default
Suggests a deliberately separate architecture if users must be shared across spaces

evals.prompt: Our login page should show tenant-specific branding in a Spaces deployment. How do I know which space a request is for and should I read acr_values tenant?
evals.expected_output: Inject ISpaceContextAccessor, GetSpaceId(); don't trust client tenant hint when space determines tenant.
assertions: Injects ISpaceContextAccessor into a scoped UI service and reads the resolved SpaceId
States Spaces do not add per-space UI/branding; you load your own space-aware settings
Advises preferring the resolved space over trusting a client-supplied tenant: acr_values hint
Notes space resolution is independent of acr_values and runs before routing

evals.prompt: A customer asks us to delete a tenant's space and later restore it. What happens to the data, and who should be allowed to do this?
evals.expected_output: Soft delete via ISpaceAdmin; pool data blocked but retained; UndeleteAsync restores; authorize and audit.
assertions: States deleting a space is a soft delete: pool data is blocked from reads and writes but retained
Mentions ISpaceAdmin.UndeleteAsync restores the space and its matching rules
Advises authorizing and auditing pool reassignment and deletion as security-boundary changes, reserved for deliberate procedures
